# Corrected copies of dependencies

The copies of the sound library (`cpal`; ADR 0733), of the call library (`webrtc-sys`, `webrtc-sys-build`, `livekit`; ADR 0733) and of the window library (`gpui-pre`, `gpui-pre-scheduler`; ADR 0757).

## `webrtc-sys` 0.3.48

`webrtc-sys-0.3.48` contains the build inputs of the published `webrtc-sys` 0.3.48 crate. The source archive has SHA-256 `9d87fa13acfe63505a0e8c1311b5dc60323a429196c4a7ba18b63de34e5cba67`. Cargo uses this copy through the workspace patch and the standalone test participant's patch.

The retained inputs are `Cargo.toml`, `build.rs`, `src/`, `include/`, `README.md` and `NOTICE.md`. The archive's development instructions, changelog, nested lockfile, original unnormalized manifest, native-library build scripts and unused native tests are not required by this build and are omitted. Copyright and licence notices in the retained inputs are unchanged.

The peer-connection destructor in `src/peer_connection.cpp` calls `Close` while both its native interface and observer still exist. The getters of the session descriptions in the same file read and copy a description on the signaling thread: the proxy of the connection returns a pointer to a description that the signaling thread can replace and free, and the published getters copied it on the calling thread (ADR 0733, test `engine::tests::the_descriptions_can_be_read_while_negotiations_replace_them`). Linux runtime initialization also registers a system-root TLS verifier from `src/system_certificate_verifier.{rs,cpp}` through the pinned binary's platform-verifier API. It uses `rustls-native-certs` to load roots and Rustls to verify chains with SSL server purpose. The build adds that bridge and its Rust dependencies only on Linux. Every throw of the crate throws `livekit_ffi::Exception` of `include/livekit/exception.h`, which owns its message; the WebRTC library for Windows, whose defines the crate uses, has `_HAS_EXCEPTIONS=0`, and with that value `std::runtime_error` keeps only a pointer to its message. The same header gives each bridge with a C++ function that returns `Result` its catch (`rust::behavior::trycatch`): an exception of the crate becomes a Rust error, and any other C++ exception ends the process with a line on standard error, written from a buffer on the stack to the handle of standard error, without an allocation and without the lock of the stream `stderr`, and followed by a line of readable names, after the Windows message box of `abort()` has been turned off; `src/exception.rs` also has test functions that hold that lock and that throw a subclass of `std::exception`. `src/exception.rs` with `src/exception.cpp` are a bridge of test functions for it. The audio processing module of `include/livekit/apm.h` processes at 48 kHz inside: the default of the WebRTC version is 32 kHz, at which the module resamples the stream of 48 kHz on the way in and out and removes everything above 16 kHz. `include/livekit/yuv_helper.h` and `src/yuv_helper.rs` add `i420_scale`, the scale of the published `I420Buffer::scale` with planes that the caller holds and does not give up, so that a received picture is scaled without a copy of its planes. `src/video_encoder_factory.cpp` and `include/livekit/video_encoder_factory.h` make every encoder through `CreateAdaptedEncoder`, which gives the simulcast adapter of WebRTC a factory of the software encoders for a format of a hardware backend, so that a hardware encoder that does not start or fails is replaced by the software encoder of its codec; `src/encoder_fallback.rs`, `src/encoder_fallback.cpp` and `include/livekit/encoder_fallback.h` are a bridge of a test function for it. ADR 0733 explains the seven corrections, their regression checks and the combined compiled-in/system trust policy. The WebRTC binary revision and every other dependency version are unchanged.

Each changed source file states in its header that it differs from the published version, and each change carries a `Modified:` comment; a new file states that it is not in the published crate. `Cargo.toml` carries its `Modified:` comment above the added dependencies.

Remove the destructor correction when the pinned upstream crate closes its native peer connection before releasing these members. Remove the description correction when a pinned upstream version copies the descriptions on the signaling thread. Remove the Linux trust correction when a pinned upstream version provides system-root verification for every default TLS adapter. Remove the exception correction when a pinned upstream version throws only exceptions that own their message, also with `_HAS_EXCEPTIONS=0`, and its bridges end the process at every other C++ exception. Remove the processing rate when the default of the pinned WebRTC version is 48 kHz or a pinned upstream version sets it, the scale when a pinned upstream version scales planes that it reads only, and the software fallback when a pinned upstream version gives the simulcast adapter a software fallback. Run the native destruction tests, window live tier and media live tier when replacing this dependency; the Linux media live tier includes the TURN TLS trust regression. Run `crates/media/tests/native_exceptions.rs` and the three exception tests of `engine::tests` (ADR 0733) on Windows when replacing this dependency or the WebRTC binary. Run `audio::processing::tests::the_module_keeps_the_microphone_above_16_khz`, `share::picture::tests::held_planes_are_scaled_as_the_call_library_scales_them`, `engine::tests::the_descriptions_can_be_read_while_negotiations_replace_them` (on Linux or macOS, ADR 0915) and the test target `encoder_fallback` of `junto-media` when replacing it.

## `webrtc-sys-build` 0.3.19

`webrtc-sys-build-0.3.19` contains the build inputs of the published `webrtc-sys-build` 0.3.19 crate, the build-script helper of `webrtc-sys` that downloads and extracts the WebRTC library. The source archive has SHA-256 `0cd4f418e16f4b7ba028e6b5c70e4f532c7d2b5ca39726d42b699f3e4591ed5c`, the checksum that the lockfile held for the registry version. The archive was made from commit `2d9f01ab1e933a86a8a5c53805ee29ee58b9be1b` of the upstream repository, directory `webrtc-sys/build` (its `.cargo_vcs_info.json`). Cargo uses this copy through the workspace patch and the standalone test participant's patch.

The retained inputs are `Cargo.toml` and `src/`. The archive's changelog, nested lockfile, original unnormalized manifest and `.cargo_vcs_info.json` are not required by this build and are omitted. The archive has no separate licence file; the crate is licensed under Apache-2.0 (its manifest), and the copyright and licence notice at the top of `src/lib.rs` is unchanged.

`src/lib.rs` is unchanged. `Cargo.toml` differs in one dependency, marked with a `Modified:` comment: `zip` 9.0.4 with its deflate decompressor (`deflate-flate2-zlib-rs`) replaces `zip` 0.6 with the feature `deflate`. The `ZipArchive::extract` of `zip` 0.6 keeps the setuid, setgid and sticky bits of an entry (RUSTSEC-2026-0367) and applies permissions through extracted symbolic links (RUSTSEC-2026-0369). ADR 0733 explains the correction and its checks. Every other dependency version is unchanged.

Remove this copy when a pinned upstream version depends on `zip` 9.0.0 or later. Build `junto-media` from an empty build directory on macOS and Linux when replacing it, so that the WebRTC archive is downloaded and extracted again, then run `cargo deny check` and the media live tier.

## `livekit` 0.9.4

`livekit-0.9.4` contains the build inputs of the published `livekit` 0.9.4 crate. The source archive has SHA-256 `4dc818741891a8179eafd4665156482761d5084fb15238c1de9c211fdb974e3e`, the checksum that the lockfile held for the registry version. The archive was made from commit `a6f93a16fa71fe811d040de175e070e233d9b1fe` of the upstream repository, directory `livekit` (its `.cargo_vcs_info.json`). Cargo uses this copy through the workspace patch and the standalone test participant's patch.

The retained inputs are `Cargo.toml`, `build.rs`, `src/` and `README.md`. The archive's changelog, nested lockfile, original unnormalized manifest, `.cargo_vcs_info.json`, examples, specifications and tests are not required by this build and are omitted. The archive has no separate licence file; the crate is licensed under Apache-2.0 (its manifest), and the copyright and licence notice at the top of each retained source file is unchanged.

Every file and every dependency version not named below are unchanged. Each changed file states in its header that it differs from the published version, and each change carries a `Modified:` comment; a new file states that it is not in the published crate. ADR 0733 explains each correction and its regression checks. Remove a correction when a pinned upstream version makes it unnecessary, and remove this copy when no correction remains. Run the tests of each remaining correction against a new version first, then the window live tier and the media live tier.

Corrections:

- Publisher negotiation queue. `src/rtc_engine/negotiation_queue.rs` is new; `src/rtc_engine/mod.rs` and `src/rtc_engine/rtc_session.rs` use it. The queue of the fast publish mode decides with one state under one lock whether a task negotiates. The published version also kept a separate flag for a running task; a request that came after the task had set the state to idle and before it cleared that flag was dropped, and every later request with it. `crates/media/tests/negotiation_queue.rs` compiles the new file and runs its tests in the workspace suite. Removed when a pinned upstream version decides the queue under one state, so that a request after the end of a negotiation always starts another one.
- Order of mute requests. `src/room/participant/in_order.rs` is new; `src/room/participant/mod.rs` uses it. The mute and unmute requests of the local tracks of a participant are sent one after the other, in the order of the changes. The published version started a task for each request; tasks that waited together for a restored connection sent in any order, and a mute that reached the media server after the unmute that followed it left the track muted there. `crates/media/tests/mute_order.rs` compiles the new file and runs its tests in the workspace suite, and reads the source of `src/room/participant/mod.rs` to check that every mute request of the participant goes through it; the media live test `sound::mute_requests_that_wait_for_a_resume_reach_the_media_server_in_their_order` checks that the requests of the participant that wait for a resume reach the media server in the order of the changes. Removed when a pinned upstream version sends the mute requests of a track in their order.
- Mute state after a resume. `src/room/participant/mod.rs`, `src/room/participant/local_participant.rs` and `src/room/mod.rs`: after each resume of the session the participant sends the mute state of each local track again, after the mute requests given before. The published version sent nothing; a mute request written to a lost signal connection before the loss was found reaches the media server late or not at all, the media server discards it when it arrives after the resume, and it does not take the mute state from the resume. The resume carries the mute flag of each publication at the time of publishing, because the SDK does not update the publication information of a local track after the publish. `crates/media/tests/mute_order.rs` reads the source of `src/room/mod.rs`, `src/room/participant/local_participant.rs` and `src/room/participant/mod.rs` to check that the room sends the mute states after each resume and that each request reads the state in its turn; the media live tests `sound::an_open_written_to_a_lost_signal_connection_reaches_the_media_server_after_the_resume` and `sound::mute_requests_that_wait_for_a_resume_reach_the_media_server_in_their_order` check the result with a media server, the second also that the request of the resume follows the requests of the changes. Removed when a pinned upstream version sends the current mute state after a resume, or when a pinned upstream version updates the publication information that the resume sends at each mute change and the pinned media server takes the mute state from the resume.
- Negotiation after the close. `src/room/mod.rs`, `src/rtc_engine/mod.rs` and `src/rtc_engine/rtc_session.rs`: the close of a room calls `RtcEngine::begin_close` before it unpublishes the tracks, and from then on the session starts no negotiation of the publisher; the close ends a wait for an answer, and `offer_publisher` makes no offer in a session that closes and takes an offer whose result comes after the close began as the end of the negotiation, with a debug line. The published version negotiated for each unpublished track while the room closed: it waited 10 seconds for an answer of a closed session, logged "peer connection is closed, cannot create offer", or logged the error "Failed to set local offer sdp: Called in wrong state: closed". The media live test `close::a_closing_room_starts_no_negotiation_and_ends_the_wait_for_an_answer`, a test program of its own, leaves a call with two published tracks while it holds the media server alone with one person in the room, and counts the negotiations that the leaves start, the failed negotiations and the offers in a closed connection; then it leaves while a negotiation waits for the answer of a paused media server, and requires that wait to end at the close. Removed when a pinned upstream version does not negotiate the publisher of a room that closes.
- Track permissions after a new connection. `src/room/mod.rs`: after a new connection of the session, `handle_restarted` sends the track permissions that the participant holds before it publishes the tracks again, and again after them. The published version sent them only after the last track was published again, and the new session at the media server, which holds no permissions, let every participant receive each of those tracks until then. `crates/media/tests/mute_order.rs` reads the source of `src/room/mod.rs` to check the order; the media live test `share::a_client_of_a_release_before_several_shares_never_receives_a_further_share` checks with a media server and a test participant of a release from before several shares that such a participant is never given a further share while the sharer connects anew (ADR 0733, ADR 0737). Removed when a pinned upstream version sends the permissions before the tracks, or the pinned media server keeps them over a new connection.

## `gpui-pre` 0.3.8 and `gpui-pre-scheduler` 0.3.8

`gpui-pre-0.3.8` and `gpui-pre-scheduler-0.3.8` contain the build inputs of the published crates of the same names, a snapshot of the `gpui` and `scheduler` crates of the upstream repository at commit `279fe070bb389b79652e52065b2f001edcc0b11b` (the `zed-rev` of their manifests). The source archives have SHA-256 `d7f0bc3ebba070f8981b3f8e905a12f47d27794a30d029e59cdb9edf7a4b3360` (`gpui-pre`) and `f4acd73345bc3c09f1b98c1b21eb4459ad8336f89bb2edcef619e11c5a08456e` (`gpui-pre-scheduler`), the checksums that the lockfile held for the registry versions. Cargo uses these copies through the workspace patch; every crate that depends on them, the platform crates and the component library included, uses the same copy.

The retained inputs of `gpui-pre` are `Cargo.toml`, `build.rs`, `src/`, `resources/` (the Windows manifest of the build script), `README.md` (the documentation of the crate includes it) and `LICENSE-APACHE`; those of `gpui-pre-scheduler` are `Cargo.toml`, `src/` and `LICENSE-APACHE`. The examples, the documents, the tests, the nested lockfiles and the original unnormalized manifests are not required by this build and are omitted; the manifest of `gpui-pre` lost the `[[example]]` and `[[test]]` sections of the omitted files and its `authors` field, which names a person (ADR 0901), and is otherwise unchanged. The crates are licensed under Apache-2.0 (their manifests and `LICENSE-APACHE`).

Every file and every dependency version not named below are unchanged. Each changed file states in its header that it differs from the published version, and each change carries a `Modified:` comment; the new file states that it is not in the published crate. ADR 0757 explains the corrections. The platform calls gpui from functions that cannot unwind (the Objective-C methods and the dispatch queue functions of macOS, the window procedures and the thread pool callbacks of Windows), so a panic in the code of the application aborted the process.

- `gpui-pre`: `src/platform.rs` and `src/window.rs` also add `activate_with_token` (see `gpui-pre-linux` below). `src/unwind.rs` is new: `catch` stops a panic, logs the 1st, 10th, 100th, and so on, panic of each callback, and gives a fixed result, `restore_on_panic` puts a value back and lets the panic continue, and the `callback…` functions wrap a callback of the platform in `catch`. `src/window.rs`: each callback that a window gives the platform stops a panic of its body; `Window::draw` resets the draw after a panic (`reset_after_a_panic_in_a_draw`: the next frame, the element stacks, the opacity, the tooltip bounds, the requested scroll, the layout engine, and the input handler of the platform window), and after three failed draws in a row draws nothing until a press of the person in `dispatch_event` (`FAILED_DRAWS_BEFORE_A_PAUSE`); `compute_layout` puts the layout engine back; `dispatch_mouse_event` puts the mouse listeners back and skips a missing one; `draw_roots` puts the prompt and the dragged view back; `dispatch_action_on_node_inner` puts the global action listeners back. `src/app.rs`: `App::update` and `App::finish_update` keep the count of nested updates and the flag of the flush right and run no effect while a panic unwinds; the update of a window, of an entity and the global action listeners put their value back; the callbacks of the application stop a panic. `src/gpui.rs`: the module, and `update_global` puts the global back. `src/subscription.rs`: `SubscriberSet::retain` puts the subscribers back. `src/platform.rs`: the methods of `PlatformInputHandler` stop a panic and return an error. `src/platform/app_menu.rs`: the menu callbacks stop a panic.
- `gpui-pre`: `src/elements/list.rs`: a list aligned at its end whose items do not fill it starts them at its top (ADR 0757, point 5, and ADR 0740). Remove the change when gpui offers that alignment; run `layout::a_short_message_list_starts_at_its_top` and the window tests of the message list (`messages::`, `scroll::`, `unread::`).
- `gpui-pre-scheduler`: `src/executor.rs` builds every task with `propagate_panic`, so that a panic of a task stops in `Runnable::run`.

Remove both copies when a pinned upstream version stops a panic in each callback that it gives the platform and in each task, and puts its state back after the panic. When replacing them, apply the corrections to the new version, then run the window tests (`cargo test -p junto-client --test app`, which include `panics::` and `gpui_panics::`), `JUNTO_TEST_NATIVE_PANICS=1 cargo test -p junto-client --test native_panics` on macOS and Windows, the window live tier and the start check of the macOS bundle.

## `gpui-pre-linux` 0.3.8

`gpui-pre-linux-0.3.8` contains the build inputs of the published `gpui-pre-linux` 0.3.8 crate, the Linux platform of gpui, a snapshot of the `gpui_linux` crate of the upstream repository at the same commit as `gpui-pre` (the `zed-rev` of its manifest). The source archive has SHA-256 `b1131746fad5c87b5de74dc9c73105655b0c820a2dd4bb247586573e7cf5720e`, the checksum that the lockfile held for the registry version. Cargo uses this copy through the workspace patch.

The retained inputs are `Cargo.toml`, `src/` and `LICENSE-APACHE`. The nested lockfile and the original unnormalized manifest are not required by this build and are omitted. The manifest is unchanged; it names no person. The crate is licensed under Apache-2.0.

Only `src/linux/wayland/window.rs` differs from the published version; it states that in its header and carries a `Modified:` comment. The Wayland window implements `activate_with_token`, which `gpui-pre` adds to `PlatformWindow`: it gives the token to `xdg_activation_v1::activate` for the surface of the window, or activates the window as before when the compositor has no activation. The published crate activated a window only with a token that the window asked for itself, which a compositor does not honour without a recent press in the window, so a press on a notification left the window without the focus. ADR 0757 explains the change and ADR 0752 the use.

Remove this copy, and the call in `gpui-pre`, when a pinned upstream version activates a window with a token that the application gives. Run the window tests and the test target `notification_focus` under `tools/linux/display.sh wayland` against a new version first.

## `cpal` 0.18.2

`cpal-0.18.2` contains the build inputs of the published `cpal` 0.18.2 crate, the sound devices of the media engine (ADR 0733). The source archive has SHA-256 `6f02e8d0327b42d3e2e4ab2119af397344eb9fc54a34bf0ddeaa1277af8681f1`, the checksum that the lockfile held for the registry version. The archive was made from commit `e1612d5d98152f8dc2a62e1b51ef7cbf4f7f26b7` of the upstream repository (its `.cargo_vcs_info.json`). Cargo uses this copy through the workspace patch.

The retained inputs are `Cargo.toml`, `build.rs`, `src/`, `examples/` (the manifest names each example), `README.md` and `LICENSE`. The archive's changelog, nested lockfile, original unnormalized manifest, `.cargo_vcs_info.json`, `.github/`, `.gitignore`, container and cross-build files, formatting settings and contribution, conduct, security and upgrade notes are not required by this build and are omitted. The copyright and licence notices in the retained inputs are unchanged.

Only `src/host/com.rs` differs from the published version; it states that in its header and carries `Modified:` comments. The published `com_initialized` entered the single-threaded apartment of COM on each Windows thread that called it and left it only when the thread ended, also on threads that `cpal` does not own: the threads of the default pool of the system, on which the window lists the devices, and the threads of the device notifications. A share with sound then failed to start with `RPC_E_CHANGED_MODE`. The copy enters no apartment: it keeps the multithreaded apartment of the process with `CoIncrementMTAUsage` and leaves the apartment of each thread as it is. ADR 0733 explains the correction and its tests.

Remove this copy when a pinned upstream version enters no apartment on threads that it does not own. Run `audio::cpal_host::tests::a_call_leaves_the_apartment_of_the_calling_thread_as_it_was` of `junto-media` and the test target `windows_capture` on Windows against a new version first, then the media live tier.
